item.title: ShikataLab - Letting an AI Agent Run My Homelab While I Travel
item.description: I’m in Korea for a couple of weeks, and I figured it was a good excuse to finally polish up the homelab back in Toronto. The catch: you can’t exactly do homelab work from a hotel room in Seoul. So most of the actual work has been done by an AI agent — Meta’s Muse, which I’ve taken to calling Jett. I send it messages from my phone between meals, it does the work, I review the diffs.

item.title: ShikataLab - The Data Story: Stretching OCI's Free Tier
item.description: Oracle’s free tier is generous with compute and weirdly stingy with disk, and that combination has shaped every storage decision in my homelab. This is the data story: what the limits actually are, the three ways I worked around them, and what’s still missing. The problem: every gigabyte counts The hard limit is 200GB of boot volume, total, across every instance in the tenancy. My main box (azamilab0, the k3s node) has a 153GB boot volume.

item.title: ShikataLab v2 - [Part 2]: ARM and Steam-Server Support
item.description: The Challenge I’m starting to hit the issue more and more where my friends and I want to play games that are primarily compiled for ARM; in general, this isn’t usually a challenge, but specific to games like Counter-Strike 2 it seems impossible to run without a lot of fuss outside of Docker The ““solution”” In the past, using stuff like Wine or Proton solved a lot of these problems for me; specifically running things like QEMU within my box to be able to emulate simple programs
